ghi_chu.mo_ta: A square-rigged, galleon-like sailing ship with an orange sail sits in the harbour. It is the main vessel in the distance, beside a low grey hull.
ghi_chu.ly_do: A square-rigged wooden sailing ship of this kind was obsolete by 1943. Gibraltar's wartime harbour held steam and motor warships, merchant ships and small craft. The ship looks like a historical or fantasy type, not one from 1943.

tra_loi.vat: A small square-rigged sailing ship in the foreground of the bay, with a larger low grey cargo or ship hull behind it
tra_loi.dac_diem: The sailing ship is small and hazy. It has a short hull, two or three masts and tan or brown square sails. A tall block-like sail or structure stands on the foremast. It looks like a galleon or carrack style. Behind it is a long, low grey hull with a red waterline stripe and a thin mast with a crosstree. I can't see any funnel on it. Both are heavily blurred by haze.
tra_loi.ly_do: Square-rigged sailing ships existed long before 1943. They were rare as warships by then, but sailing vessels and merchant hulls were still present. The grey hull behind is a conventional steel ship of a kind that existed in 1943.
